_comment: One page for every test and comparison sheet (user, Oct 21: 'one artifact, with collapsible sections based on tests you're running ... with clues as to what i should be looking at, when'). Newest first within each status. status: needs-you | running | done | settled | superseded. Build + publish: python3 tools/house/test_board.py (then Artifact publish ~/.cache/home-alone-board/test-board.html to the board URL).
decisions: Van at night reads dark: only the street lamp behind it lights it. Add a fill light like the film's movie lighting?
Night white balance default: you leaned to -57 (cooler). Try it in the app with [ and ].
Front-yard trees: where the film puts them (right of the portico) or where the laser survey puts them (left)?

tests.title: Night speed: what's expensive in the foyer, kitchen and hall
tests.when: Now: the Mac is free. About 3 min to build, 9 min to run; leave the Mac alone.
tests.what: The heavy night rooms still run 23-29 fps at the new full-screen default. This switches off one costly effect at a time (fog, reflections, ambient occlusion, contact and lamp shadows, glass, sheers, the foyer mirror) so you can trade look against speed.
commands: HA_PERF_APP=$HOME/.cache/home-alone-perf/build/HomeAlonePerfB.app HA_DISPLAY="Studio Display" HA_PERF_ARGS='-perfab -perfrounds 1 -perfbasescale auto -perfdn night -perfposes foyer-night,kitchen-night,hall-night -perfvariants off=Volumetrics;off=SSR;off=SSAO;off=ContactShadows;off=ShadowMaps;off=TransparentObjects;off=PlanarProbe;hide=Glass;hide=Voile;lowres=all;fit=1;range=0.7' tools/house/perf_probe.sh run fs-nightB
tests.app: HomeAlonePerfB.app (full screen on the Studio Display at the new default: 2048x1152, scaled to the panel)
look: Nothing to look at until the run is in: the sheet lands here with FPS on every tile.
Then: each column is one effect off or cheaper. The 'off' columns (fog, reflections, AO, contact shadows, lamp shadows, all glass and sheers, mirror) show what an effect costs, not a look to ship.

Pick from the last five columns (no glass, no sheers, low-res glass and sheers, lamp ranges fitted to rooms, ranges x0.7): those are candidates. Watch the sheers' softness and light spilling through doorways.

tests.title: Front brick: upstairs darker than downstairs
tests.when: Prepared, not built. Next: one full build + bake (about 40 min, Mac busy) after your perf test, on the coordinator's go.
tests.what: Your catch, now measured: tools/house/brick_storeys.py compares the upstairs brick with the ground-floor brick at your 06:45 spot (gate: within 5%). NB8 fails every tile: overcast upstairs 0.71 of downstairs in the centre, 0.78 at the left wing; night 0.63 in the centre; sunny 0.95. Cause: every probe outside the rooms is switched off, so the front wall takes its stored light from the rooms behind it, and upstairs that is Marina's bigger, dark upstairs. Fix prepared (BakeLighting): probes outside the film's house stay on and are tagged Exterior, rooms Interior, Marina's strip both; outside walls read only Exterior probes, room surfaces only Interior ones (Unity 6 probe rendering layers), so rooms should not change. Caveat: with the stored light off entirely the upstairs is still 0.81-0.85 of downstairs on our tile (film 6399: 0.94-1.10), so something besides the probes may remain.
look: Until the build: nothing new. The sheet below is the before.
After: upstairs and downstairs brick the same red as in film 6399, by day and at night.
Foyer and living room at night must look unchanged.

tests.title: Full-screen speed: why the Studio Display was slow
tests.what: Lowering the internal resolution (dynamic resolution) was itself the main cost: it stalled the graphics driver for most of each frame. The new default is full screen at a fixed 2048x1152, stretched to the display, with dynamic resolution off; P steps screen sizes. It runs in the next build.
